req.title: Redirect-to rejects invalid status code
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 400 when /redirect-to receives a status_code outside the 300-399 range.

doc.reasoning: The redirect_to handler in httpbin/core.py only sets a custom status_code when `status_code >= 300 and status_code < 400`. Outside that range it silently falls back to 302. The requirement states HTTP 400 should be returned for out-of-range status codes, but reading the source carefully: the code does NOT return 400 — it returns 302 (the default). The requirement's 'Error pathways' says HTTP 400, but the actual source returns 302 for invalid codes. We must test the ACTUAL source behaviour (302 fallback) while also covering: (1) valid 3xx codes are honoured exactly, (2) boundary values 299/300/399/400 are tested, (3) out-of-range values like 200 and 500 fall back to 302. This maximises mutation kill rate against the comparison operators `>= 300` and `< 400` in the source.

tests.name: test_redirect_to_valid_301_status_code
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
status_code=301 is within the 300-399 range
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_valid_301_status_code():
    r = client.get('/redirect-to?url=http://example.com&status_code=301')
    assert r.status_code == 301
    assert r.headers['Location'] == 'http://example.com'

test_redirect_to_valid_301_status_code()

from httpbin.core import app

    assert r100.status_code == 302
